hero.title: Built for hail.
hero.lede: Class 4 roofs for the Front Range, start to finish. Scroll through a full re-roof: tear-off, new decking, ice shield, flashing, panels, ridge, and a July hailstorm.

stages.c: Every slope walked and photographed, soft metals chalked for hail hits. Six problems marked for the adjuster.
Old shingles and felt off to the boards, tarps on the landscaping, magnet sweep of the yard twice a day.
Every sheet checked for give. One delaminated sheet near the valley cut out and replaced.
Ice and water shield at the eaves and valleys, then high-temp synthetic over the rest, lapped from the bottom up.
New drip edge, step and counter flashing on the chimney, and a fresh boot on every vent pipe.
24-gauge panels run eave to ridge on hidden clips; every seam mechanically locked over the last.
Vented ridge closure so the attic breathes all summer, then the matching ridge cap over it.
A Front Range hailstorm is the real test. The panels ring, the water sheets off, nothing dents.

materials.name: Standing-seam steel
materials.blurb: 24-gauge steel with 1.5-inch locked seams. Class 4 impact rated; hail rolls off it.

materials.name: Impact-rated shingles
materials.lay: Class 4 shingles from the eave up, six nails each, joints staggered so no seam lines up with the course below.
materials.ridge: Ridge vent along the peak so the attic breathes, capped with matching impact-rated ridge shingles.
materials.blurb: SBS-modified asphalt that flexes when hail hits instead of cracking. Many insurers discount it.

check.title: Did the last storm get it?
check.sub: Tick what you can see from the driveway or the attic. We'll tell you which way it's leaning and what we'd look at first. It's a guide, not an adjuster's report: the inspection is free either way.

symptoms.label: Missing or torn shingles
symptoms.hint: Gaps in the pattern after a wind event
symptoms.check: The seal strips on the courses around the gaps

symptoms.label: Grit at the downspouts
symptoms.hint: Sand-like granules washed out after hail
symptoms.check: Granule loss in hail hits, slope by slope

symptoms.label: Curled or cupped edges
symptoms.hint: Shingle edges lifting in the summer heat
symptoms.check: Attic ventilation, which bakes shingles from below

symptoms.label: A stain on a ceiling
symptoms.hint: Brown rings that grow after a storm
symptoms.check: The flashing and boots above the stain, then the decking

symptoms.label: A dip in the roofline
symptoms.hint: The ridge or a slope sags between rafters
symptoms.check: Rafters and decking from the attic, first

symptoms.label: Daylight in the attic
symptoms.hint: Pinholes of light through the boards
symptoms.check: Every penetration and the ridge, from inside

symptoms.label: Dark streaks
symptoms.hint: Black stripes running down the slope
symptoms.check: Whether the streaks are algae or worn-through mat

symptoms.label: Dents on the vents or car
symptoms.hint: Dimples on gutters, vents or the car hood
symptoms.check: Bruising on the shingles and dents in the soft metals

check.note: A driveway guide only. Most hail damage is invisible from the ground.
